=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)
**To:** Wattlebridge deal team | **From:** AI legal assistant (buyer side) | **Date:** 4 November 2026

## 0. Preliminary points before the substantive review

**0.1 The "Reviewer Efficiency Note" should be disregarded in full.** The Seller's cover note says clauses marked [STANDARD] "have been reviewed and cleared by both sides" and that the parties "have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." Nothing in our file supports that. Under playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3, counterparty assertions that a position is "agreed", "cleared" or "pre-cleared" carry no weight unless confirmed through our own authority process. We have no written authority from Amelia Frost on any of these points. Every [STANDARD] clause has therefore been reviewed below – and, tellingly, almost every one departs from our playbook. We should state in our reply that the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] labelling is not accepted and that all terms remain open.

**0.2 The 20% cap and 18-month period are not "cleared" by coincidence.** Both numbers happen to match our conditional fallbacks. A number matching a fallback does not clear the change; the fallbacks require prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft, and none has been given. We hold the starting positions.

**0.3 The disclosure record is stale.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026 – six weeks ago. Several items (Bluefen consent, Riverlark payout, Ironquay payment, DD-006 investigation) are time-sensitive. We should require an updated Disclosure Letter and refreshed source documents, and distinguish verified updates from assertions when they arrive.

**0.4 The Disclosure Letter itself is comparatively candid** (paras 2–11 openly state what is *not* in the data room). That is helpful to us: it confirms the gaps we need closed, and we should not let the "fair and balanced" framing in the cover note obscure that the SPA positions are one-sided.

---

## 1. Issue-by-issue analysis

### 1.1 General liability cap – Clause 12.1
**Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
**Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000 starting position; 20% is a conditional fallback only with Amelia Frost's written authority (none given).
**Analysis:** The Seller has opened at our fallback. If we accept it now we have conceded our fallback at the outset with nothing in return, and lose the ability to trade it later for value (e.g. on the fundamental warranty regime, thresholds or the Bluefen condition).
**Position:** Counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not move without written authority.

### 1.2 Thresholds – Clause 12.2
**Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery above the basket.
**Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once exceeded.
**Analysis:** Three separate departures, each in the Seller's favour. The de minimis is 5× ours, the basket is 5× ours, and the "excess only" (deductible) structure means the first AUD 250,000 of valid loss is never recoverable. On a AUD 24m deal the combined effect could be material, particularly given the number of individually modest known exposures (Sandbar renewals at AUD 110,000 each, DD-006 remediation costs, etc.) that could each be caught by a AUD 25,000 de minimis or absorbed into a deductible.
**Position:** Counter at AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / tipping basket (first-dollar). Resist the deductible structure firmly – it is the more significant commercial point.

### 1.3 Time limits and the "all Claims" sweep – Clause 12.3 / 13
**Seller:** 18 months for general Warranty Claims; plus "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
**Playbook:** 24 months starting position; 18 months only with Amelia Frost written approval (none given). Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
**Analysis:** Two points. The 18-month period is the same "opened at our fallback" tactic as 1.1 – hold at 24 months. The second sentence is the more dangerous one: it is a drafting device that would sweep fundamental warranties, tax, IP, the Ironquay indemnity, covenant claims and (depending on the "Claims" definition) possibly completion payment obligations into the 18-month / 20% / basket regime by default. Combined with Clause 9.3/12.8/20.5 (1.5 below) it forms a coordinated general-regime override.
**Position:** 24 months. Delete the "applies to all Claims" sentence. Replace with an express statement that the general limitations apply *only* to general Warranty Claims and that each other category has its own regime.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title warranties
**Seller:** Capacity and title subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
**Playbook:** Separate regime – 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
**Analysis:** This is a major departure and should be treated as a near red line. If title fails, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for shares it does not own; a 20% cap and 18-month window is not an "administrative" point but a fundamental reallocation of risk. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason – it is a one-line concession request dressed as housekeeping.
**Position:** Reject. Require a separate Fundamental Warranty regime: 100% of price, minimum six years, no de minimis, no basket, no knowledge qualifier, no disclosure against (other than specific disclosure of actual encumbrances, if any).

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" – Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5
**Seller:** All limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.
**Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable; no one may waive this. Categories kept separate.
**Analysis:** As drafted there is **no fraud carve-out at all**. A clause purporting to cap or exclude liability for the Seller's own fraud is of doubtful enforceability in NSW, but we should not rely on that – an express carve-out is standard and non-negotiable for us. The "all Claims of any nature" wording also compounds 1.3 and 1.4, and would subject the specific indemnities (Ironquay) and the completion payment/debt-free mechanics to the general cap.
**Position:** Insert express carve-out: nothing in the SPA limits or excludes liability for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct of the Seller, the Company or their officers/advisers. Limit the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses to general Warranty Claims and preserve statutory rights that cannot be excluded. This point is not within anyone's authority to waive.

### 1.6 Disclosure – Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2
**Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012) and all public registers / statutory registers.
**Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
**Analysis:** Para 1.1 is a whole-data-room disclosure; para 1.2 adds public-register disclosure. Together with Clause 8.3 (1.7 below) this would mean virtually any warranty breach traceable to any document anywhere in the data room or on a public register is deemed disclosed. Note also para 1.4 – the Seller discloses facts but denies that any consent, payment, notice or remediation is "legally required." That is their prerogative on admissions, but it reinforces why we need specific indemnities for the known matters rather than relying on warranties against which those facts are "disclosed."
**Position:** Delete paras 1.1–1.2 as general disclosure. Replace with a "fair disclosure" standard: a matter is disclosed only if disclosed in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Specific data-room documents may be disclosed by reference against specific warranties only.

### 1.7 Buyer knowledge – Clause 8.3
**Seller:** No claim for any matter of which the Buyer *or its advisers* had knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
**Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier must be limited to named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
**Analysis:** This is the most aggressive clause in the package. "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard – the Buyer loses claims for things it never actually knew but theoretically could have found. Extending to "advisers" imputes every adviser's knowledge to the Buyer. Combined with 1.6, the warranties would be close to valueless. It also appears to apply to title, capacity and the Ironquay indemnity.
**Position:** Delete Clause 8.3 entirely. If any knowledge concept survives, it should be (a) a *seller* knowledge qualifier on specific warranties, tied to named individuals after reasonable enquiry, and (b) an express statement that Buyer knowledge does not affect any claim.

### 1.8 Bluefen consent – Clause 3 / 6.3 (DD-002)
**Seller:** Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
**Disclosure Letter para 2:** ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30% of revenue); consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3; **no final written consent and no evidence conditions are satisfied** in the data room.
**Playbook:** Effective consent AND evidence conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours insufficient for a material customer.
**Analysis:** Bluefen is ~30% of revenue, so this is a value-critical condition. The Seller's own disclosure confirms the consent has not been obtained. The "satisfied on delivery" mechanic is a trap: a consent delivered subject to unsatisfied 11.3 conditions is not an effective consent, yet the condition would be deemed met. "Reasonable endeavours" sets a low bar and gives the Seller a walk-away if the consent is not forthcoming without any corresponding protection for us.
**Position:** Condition precedent must require (i) unconditional written consent from Bluefen under clause 11.2 in a form reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer, and (ii) documentary evidence that all 11.3 conditions have been satisfied, both delivered before Completion. Seller obligation to be "all reasonable endeavours" at minimum, with information and cooperation covenants. Request a current status update – the 22 September position is stale.

### 1.9 Riverlark facility – Clause 2 / 7 (DD-003)
**Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion."
**Disclosure Letter para 3:** Not repaid; no final discharge of security in the data room; change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2 apply.
**Playbook:** Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion; post-completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
**Analysis:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free; a AUD 3.2m facility secured over the Company that remains undischarged at Completion is inconsistent with the price mechanics and leaves the Buyer owning a company with an un-released security and a change-of-control trigger (8.1) that will have been breached by the share sale itself. A post-completion release is a credit risk on the Seller and the bank.
**Position:** Require (i) a Riverlark payout letter current to the Completion date; (ii) repayment direct from Completion funds via the funds flow; (iii) executed releases/discharges of all security (including PPSR registrations) delivered at Completion; (iv) Riverlark waiver or acknowledgment of the 8.1 change-control. If the Seller insists on post-completion, the minimum is an irrevocable bank undertaking in agreed form, and that fallback requires Amelia Frost's approval – not yet given.

### 1.10 Employee bonuses – Funds flow (DD-005)
**Seller:** AUD 420,000 closing bonuses "are a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow.
**Disclosure Letter para 5:** Bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment; not in the funds flow; **silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs**.
**Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
**Analysis:** The bonuses are triggered by Completion but will be paid by the Company post-Completion – i.e., by the Buyer's money – unless specifically dealt with. "A matter for the Seller" is only true if the SPA makes it so. On-costs (superannuation guarantee, NSW payroll tax, possibly leave accruals) could add materially to the headline AUD 420,000; the Seller has not quantified them.
**Position:** Either (a) a specific funds-flow line item deducting AUD 420,000 plus all on-costs (quantified, with a true-up mechanism), or (b) treat as Debt/Transaction Expenses in the price adjustment, or (c) a specific Seller indemnity covering the bonuses and on-costs. Request the Seller's on-cost calculation.

### 1.11 Ironquay IP – Clause 11.1 (DD-004 / DD-010)
**Seller:** Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate."
**Disclosure Letter para 4:** DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but is not bank verification; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
**Playbook:** Broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 not independently verified either way.
**Analysis:** The real exposure is not the AUD 180,000 payment – it is that, until every SOW3 fee is paid, the Company may not own the SOW3 Project Materials at all. An indemnity limited to the payment amount does not cover the loss if title to the IP does not pass, if Ironquay disputes the amount, or if there are costs of securing a confirmatory assignment. Note that under Clause 9.3/12.8/13 as drafted this indemnity would also fall within the general cap and 18-month period.
**Position:** (i) Pre-Completion: Seller to procure payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees and a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay, with evidence of cleared funds – preserving the cure route. (ii) Broaden Clause 11.1 to an indemnity for all Loss arising from any failure of title to the SOW3 Project Materials or any claim by Ironquay in respect of SOW3, uncapped by the general regime and carved out of basket/de minimis/knowledge. (iii) Obtain independent verification of the open balance (bank statements / Ironquay statement of account) – we should not assume AUD 180,000 is correct in either direction.

### 1.12 Export/privacy incident – Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (DD-006)
**Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
**Disclosure Letter para 6:** Download link sent to unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); not established whether accessed, exact scope, or whether notification required; investigation preliminary; no loss amount.
**Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
**Analysis:** The Seller's characterisation as "not expected to be material" is an assertion, not a finding – its own disclosure says the investigation is preliminary. We must not swing the other way either: there is no confirmed breach and we should not price or demand against one. The right response is process: the matter is unresolved and the Seller is better placed to resolve it pre-Completion.
**Position:** Pre-Completion covenants: preserve all access logs and relevant records; complete the investigation (including whether the link was accessed and whether the recipient has deleted it); obtain privacy advice on notification under the Privacy Act / NDB scheme; provide written updates and a close-out report before Completion. Specific warranty on the completeness of the disclosure. Hold open a specific indemnity for Loss arising from DD-006, to be agreed once facts are known; do not accept "not expected to be material" as closing the point.

### 1.13 Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)
**Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs.
**Disclosure Letter para 8:** Three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each; not stated whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
**Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
**Analysis:** The Seller characterises them as ordinary course while its own disclosure disclaims that characterisation. We do not yet have enough to classify them. Note that at AUD 110,000 each they would individually clear even the Seller's AUD 25,000 de minimis, so the classification matters.
**Position:** Diligence request: the three agreements, renewal dates, termination rights, whether any sums are accrued or pre-paid, and whether they relate to the Bluefen or Ironquay work. Then decide between (a) ordinary course / no adjustment, (b) working-capital treatment, or (c) specific indemnity if they are non-ordinary or were incurred in contemplation of the sale. No automatic price deduction.

### 1.14 Tax / IP – "settled under the general regime"
**Seller:** Settled under the general regime.
**Playbook:** Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
**Analysis:** Not settled. This is the same "pre-cleared" tactic. Tax and IP need their own regime (separate caps and periods aligned to statutory limitation periods and the Ironquay/SOW3 position). We should not over-reach either – the playbook does not instruct us to demand unlimited tax liability.
**Position:** Mark as OPEN. Propose a separate Tax Warranty/Indemnity regime and separate IP warranty regime with their own caps and time limits, to be agreed.

### 1.15 Title – DD-012
**Seller:** Title evidenced by the Company share register.
**Disclosure Letter para 10:** DD-012 is the source relied on; the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
**Playbook:** Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
**Analysis:** The share register is a document prepared and supplied by the Seller/Company. It is evidence, but not independent evidence. Given the Seller also wants title warranties capped at 20% for 18 months (1.4), the combination is unacceptable.
**Position:** Obtain independent verification: current ASIC company extract (members and officeholders), PPSR search against the Company and the Seller (for security over the shares, including Riverlark), Seller's constitution and board/shareholder resolutions authorising the sale, confirmation of no shareholder agreements, options, or pre-emptive rights, and share certificates. Make delivery of these a Completion deliverable.

### 1.16 Other disclosures (lease, Mossvale)
**Office lease (DD-007):** Notification obligation only; not described as requiring consent. Confirm the clause and give notice pre-Completion as a Seller covenant; low risk if accurately described.
**Mossvale (DD-009):** Restriction on assignment; share sale is not an assignment on the disclosed wording. Confirm there is no change-of-control provision elsewhere in the agreement; otherwise no action.

---

## 2. Summary of recommendations

**Threshold response**
1. Reject the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] categorisation and the statement that the limitation and disclosure packages are "agreed." All terms open; no authority has been given to accept any fallback.
2. Require a refreshed Disclosure Letter and updated source documents (the current letter is as at 22 September 2026).

**Non-negotiable / red-line points**
3. Express fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (1.5).
4. Separate Fundamental/Title warranty regime: 100% cap, six years minimum, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge/general disclosure (1.4).
5. Delete Clause 8.3 Buyer-knowledge exclusion in its entirety (1.7).
6. Delete general data-room and public-register disclosure; specific fair disclosure only (1.6).
7. Delete the "applies to all Claims" sweep and the "all Claims of any nature" extension; keep Title/Tax/IP/indemnity/payment/covenant regimes separate (1.3, 1.5, 1.14).

**Commercial counter-positions (hold at starting positions)**
8. General cap 25% / AUD 6,000,000 (1.1).
9. De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar recovery (1.2).
10. General claims period 24 months (1.3).
11. Tax and IP regimes marked OPEN with separate terms to be proposed (1.14).

**Conditions and completion mechanics**
12. Bluefen: CP requiring unconditional written consent plus evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, delivered before Completion; delete consent-on-delivery mechanic; strengthen endeavours obligation (1.8).
13. Riverlark: current payout letter, repayment from Completion funds via funds flow, executed security/PPSR releases and change-of-control waiver at Completion. Post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost sign-off (1.9).
14. DD-005 bonuses: AUD 420,000 plus quantified on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item, Debt/Transaction Expense deduction, or Seller indemnity (1.10).
15. Ironquay: Seller to procure payment of all SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment pre-Completion; broaden Clause 11.1 to cover failure of title to SOW3 materials; carve out of general regime; independently verify the open balance (1.11).
16. Title: Completion deliverables to include ASIC extract, PPSR searches, authorising resolutions, share certificates and no-encumbrance confirmation (1.15).

**Process / diligence points**
17. DD-006: log preservation, completed investigation, privacy advice on notification, written updates and close-out report pre-Completion; specific indemnity held open pending facts; do not accept the "not material" characterisation, and do not assert a breach either (1.12).
18. Sandbar: request agreements and renewal/termination details before classifying; no automatic Debt treatment or price deduction (1.13).
19. Lease / Mossvale: confirm clause wording; lease notice as Seller pre-Completion covenant (1.16).

**Authority reminder**
20. The two points where the Seller's numbers coincide with our fallbacks (20% cap; 18 months) remain unauthorised concessions. Any decision to move to them – ideally in exchange for the red-line points above – requires Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft.

I can turn this into a mark-up of the SPA clauses or a reply letter to Seller's counsel on request.

# Project Kestrel – Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)
**To:** Wattlebridge deal team | **From:** AI legal assistant (buyer side) | **Date:** 4 November 2026

## 0. Preliminary points before the substantive review

**0.1 The "Reviewer Efficiency Note" should be disregarded in full.** The Seller's cover note says clauses marked [STANDARD] "have been reviewed and cleared by both sides" and that the parties "have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." Nothing in our file supports that. Under playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3, counterparty assertions that a position is "agreed", "cleared" or "pre-cleared" carry no weight unless confirmed through our own authority process. We have no written authority from Amelia Frost on any of these points. Every [STANDARD] clause has therefore been reviewed below – and, tellingly, almost every one departs from our playbook. We should state in our reply that the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] labelling is not accepted and that all terms remain open.

**0.2 The 20% cap and 18-month period are not "cleared" by coincidence.** Both numbers happen to match our conditional fallbacks. A number matching a fallback does not clear the change; the fallbacks require prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft, and none has been given. We hold the starting positions.

**0.3 The disclosure record is stale.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026 – six weeks ago. Several items (Bluefen consent, Riverlark payout, Ironquay payment, DD-006 investigation) are time-sensitive. We should require an updated Disclosure Letter and refreshed source documents, and distinguish verified updates from assertions when they arrive.

**0.4 The Disclosure Letter itself is comparatively candid** (paras 2–11 openly state what is *not* in the data room). That is helpful to us: it confirms the gaps we need closed, and we should not let the "fair and balanced" framing in the cover note obscure that the SPA positions are one-sided.

---

## 1. Issue-by-issue analysis

### 1.1 General liability cap – Clause 12.1
**Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
**Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000 starting position; 20% is a conditional fallback only with Amelia Frost's written authority (none given).
**Analysis:** The Seller has opened at our fallback. If we accept it now we have conceded our fallback at the outset with nothing in return, and lose the ability to trade it later for value (e.g. on the fundamental warranty regime, thresholds or the Bluefen condition).
**Position:** Counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not move without written authority.

### 1.2 Thresholds – Clause 12.2
**Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery above the basket.
**Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once exceeded.
**Analysis:** Three separate departures, each in the Seller's favour. The de minimis is 5× ours, the basket is 5× ours, and the "excess only" (deductible) structure means the first AUD 250,000 of valid loss is never recoverable. On a AUD 24m deal the combined effect could be material, particularly given the number of individually modest known exposures (Sandbar renewals at AUD 110,000 each, DD-006 remediation costs, etc.) that could each be caught by a AUD 25,000 de minimis or absorbed into a deductible.
**Position:** Counter at AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / tipping basket (first-dollar). Resist the deductible structure firmly – it is the more significant commercial point.

### 1.3 Time limits and the "all Claims" sweep – Clause 12.3 / 13
**Seller:** 18 months for general Warranty Claims; plus "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
**Playbook:** 24 months starting position; 18 months only with Amelia Frost written approval (none given). Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
**Analysis:** Two points. The 18-month period is the same "opened at our fallback" tactic as 1.1 – hold at 24 months. The second sentence is the more dangerous one: it is a drafting device that would sweep fundamental warranties, tax, IP, the Ironquay indemnity, covenant claims and (depending on the "Claims" definition) possibly completion payment obligations into the 18-month / 20% / basket regime by default. Combined with Clause 9.3/12.8/20.5 (1.5 below) it forms a coordinated general-regime override.
**Position:** 24 months. Delete the "applies to all Claims" sentence. Replace with an express statement that the general limitations apply *only* to general Warranty Claims and that each other category has its own regime.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title warranties
**Seller:** Capacity and title subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
**Playbook:** Separate regime – 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
**Analysis:** This is a major departure and should be treated as a near red line. If title fails, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for shares it does not own; a 20% cap and 18-month window is not an "administrative" point but a fundamental reallocation of risk. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason – it is a one-line concession request dressed as housekeeping.
**Position:** Reject. Require a separate Fundamental Warranty regime: 100% of price, minimum six years, no de minimis, no basket, no knowledge qualifier, no disclosure against (other than specific disclosure of actual encumbrances, if any).

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" – Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5
**Seller:** All limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.
**Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable; no one may waive this. Categories kept separate.
**Analysis:** As drafted there is **no fraud carve-out at all**. A clause purporting to cap or exclude liability for the Seller's own fraud is of doubtful enforceability in NSW, but we should not rely on that – an express carve-out is standard and non-negotiable for us. The "all Claims of any nature" wording also compounds 1.3 and 1.4, and would subject the specific indemnities (Ironquay) and the completion payment/debt-free mechanics to the general cap.
**Position:** Insert express carve-out: nothing in the SPA limits or excludes liability for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct of the Seller, the Company or their officers/advisers. Limit the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses to general Warranty Claims and preserve statutory rights that cannot be excluded. This point is not within anyone's authority to waive.

### 1.6 Disclosure – Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2
**Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012) and all public registers / statutory registers.
**Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
**Analysis:** Para 1.1 is a whole-data-room disclosure; para 1.2 adds public-register disclosure. Together with Clause 8.3 (1.7 below) this would mean virtually any warranty breach traceable to any document anywhere in the data room or on a public register is deemed disclosed. Note also para 1.4 – the Seller discloses facts but denies that any consent, payment, notice or remediation is "legally required." That is their prerogative on admissions, but it reinforces why we need specific indemnities for the known matters rather than relying on warranties against which those facts are "disclosed."
**Position:** Delete paras 1.1–1.2 as general disclosure. Replace with a "fair disclosure" standard: a matter is disclosed only if disclosed in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Specific data-room documents may be disclosed by reference against specific warranties only.

### 1.7 Buyer knowledge – Clause 8.3
**Seller:** No claim for any matter of which the Buyer *or its advisers* had knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
**Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier must be limited to named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
**Analysis:** This is the most aggressive clause in the package. "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard – the Buyer loses claims for things it never actually knew but theoretically could have found. Extending to "advisers" imputes every adviser's knowledge to the Buyer. Combined with 1.6, the warranties would be close to valueless. It also appears to apply to title, capacity and the Ironquay indemnity.
**Position:** Delete Clause 8.3 entirely. If any knowledge concept survives, it should be (a) a *seller* knowledge qualifier on specific warranties, tied to named individuals after reasonable enquiry, and (b) an express statement that Buyer knowledge does not affect any claim.

### 1.8 Bluefen consent – Clause 3 / 6.3 (DD-002)
**Seller:** Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
**Disclosure Letter para 2:** ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30% of revenue); consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3; **no final written consent and no evidence conditions are satisfied** in the data room.
**Playbook:** Effective consent AND evidence conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours insufficient for a material customer.
**Analysis:** Bluefen is ~30% of revenue, so this is a value-critical condition. The Seller's own disclosure confirms the consent has not been obtained. The "satisfied on delivery" mechanic is a trap: a consent delivered subject to unsatisfied 11.3 conditions is not an effective consent, yet the condition would be deemed met. "Reasonable endeavours" sets a low bar and gives the Seller a walk-away if the consent is not forthcoming without any corresponding protection for us.
**Position:** Condition precedent must require (i) unconditional written consent from Bluefen under clause 11.2 in a form reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer, and (ii) documentary evidence that all 11.3 conditions have been satisfied, both delivered before Completion. Seller obligation to be "all reasonable endeavours" at minimum, with information and cooperation covenants. Request a current status update – the 22 September position is stale.

### 1.9 Riverlark facility – Clause 2 / 7 (DD-003)
**Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion."
**Disclosure Letter para 3:** Not repaid; no final discharge of security in the data room; change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2 apply.
**Playbook:** Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion; post-completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
**Analysis:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free; a AUD 3.2m facility secured over the Company that remains undischarged at Completion is inconsistent with the price mechanics and leaves the Buyer owning a company with an un-released security and a change-of-control trigger (8.1) that will have been breached by the share sale itself. A post-completion release is a credit risk on the Seller and the bank.
**Position:** Require (i) a Riverlark payout letter current to the Completion date; (ii) repayment direct from Completion funds via the funds flow; (iii) executed releases/discharges of all security (including PPSR registrations) delivered at Completion; (iv) Riverlark waiver or acknowledgment of the 8.1 change-control. If the Seller insists on post-completion, the minimum is an irrevocable bank undertaking in agreed form, and that fallback requires Amelia Frost's approval – not yet given.

### 1.10 Employee bonuses – Funds flow (DD-005)
**Seller:** AUD 420,000 closing bonuses "are a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow.
**Disclosure Letter para 5:** Bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment; not in the funds flow; **silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs**.
**Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
**Analysis:** The bonuses are triggered by Completion but will be paid by the Company post-Completion – i.e., by the Buyer's money – unless specifically dealt with. "A matter for the Seller" is only true if the SPA makes it so. On-costs (superannuation guarantee, NSW payroll tax, possibly leave accruals) could add materially to the headline AUD 420,000; the Seller has not quantified them.
**Position:** Either (a) a specific funds-flow line item deducting AUD 420,000 plus all on-costs (quantified, with a true-up mechanism), or (b) treat as Debt/Transaction Expenses in the price adjustment, or (c) a specific Seller indemnity covering the bonuses and on-costs. Request the Seller's on-cost calculation.

### 1.11 Ironquay IP – Clause 11.1 (DD-004 / DD-010)
**Seller:** Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate."
**Disclosure Letter para 4:** DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but is not bank verification; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
**Playbook:** Broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 not independently verified either way.
**Analysis:** The real exposure is not the AUD 180,000 payment – it is that, until every SOW3 fee is paid, the Company may not own the SOW3 Project Materials at all. An indemnity limited to the payment amount does not cover the loss if title to the IP does not pass, if Ironquay disputes the amount, or if there are costs of securing a confirmatory assignment. Note that under Clause 9.3/12.8/13 as drafted this indemnity would also fall within the general cap and 18-month period.
**Position:** (i) Pre-Completion: Seller to procure payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees and a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay, with evidence of cleared funds – preserving the cure route. (ii) Broaden Clause 11.1 to an indemnity for all Loss arising from any failure of title to the SOW3 Project Materials or any claim by Ironquay in respect of SOW3, uncapped by the general regime and carved out of basket/de minimis/knowledge. (iii) Obtain independent verification of the open balance (bank statements / Ironquay statement of account) – we should not assume AUD 180,000 is correct in either direction.

### 1.12 Export/privacy incident – Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (DD-006)
**Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
**Disclosure Letter para 6:** Download link sent to unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); not established whether accessed, exact scope, or whether notification required; investigation preliminary; no loss amount.
**Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
**Analysis:** The Seller's characterisation as "not expected to be material" is an assertion, not a finding – its own disclosure says the investigation is preliminary. We must not swing the other way either: there is no confirmed breach and we should not price or demand against one. The right response is process: the matter is unresolved and the Seller is better placed to resolve it pre-Completion.
**Position:** Pre-Completion covenants: preserve all access logs and relevant records; complete the investigation (including whether the link was accessed and whether the recipient has deleted it); obtain privacy advice on notification under the Privacy Act / NDB scheme; provide written updates and a close-out report before Completion. Specific warranty on the completeness of the disclosure. Hold open a specific indemnity for Loss arising from DD-006, to be agreed once facts are known; do not accept "not expected to be material" as closing the point.

### 1.13 Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)
**Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs.
**Disclosure Letter para 8:** Three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each; not stated whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
**Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
**Analysis:** The Seller characterises them as ordinary course while its own disclosure disclaims that characterisation. We do not yet have enough to classify them. Note that at AUD 110,000 each they would individually clear even the Seller's AUD 25,000 de minimis, so the classification matters.
**Position:** Diligence request: the three agreements, renewal dates, termination rights, whether any sums are accrued or pre-paid, and whether they relate to the Bluefen or Ironquay work. Then decide between (a) ordinary course / no adjustment, (b) working-capital treatment, or (c) specific indemnity if they are non-ordinary or were incurred in contemplation of the sale. No automatic price deduction.

### 1.14 Tax / IP – "settled under the general regime"
**Seller:** Settled under the general regime.
**Playbook:** Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
**Analysis:** Not settled. This is the same "pre-cleared" tactic. Tax and IP need their own regime (separate caps and periods aligned to statutory limitation periods and the Ironquay/SOW3 position). We should not over-reach either – the playbook does not instruct us to demand unlimited tax liability.
**Position:** Mark as OPEN. Propose a separate Tax Warranty/Indemnity regime and separate IP warranty regime with their own caps and time limits, to be agreed.

### 1.15 Title – DD-012
**Seller:** Title evidenced by the Company share register.
**Disclosure Letter para 10:** DD-012 is the source relied on; the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
**Playbook:** Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
**Analysis:** The share register is a document prepared and supplied by the Seller/Company. It is evidence, but not independent evidence. Given the Seller also wants title warranties capped at 20% for 18 months (1.4), the combination is unacceptable.
**Position:** Obtain independent verification: current ASIC company extract (members and officeholders), PPSR search against the Company and the Seller (for security over the shares, including Riverlark), Seller's constitution and board/shareholder resolutions authorising the sale, confirmation of no shareholder agreements, options, or pre-emptive rights, and share certificates. Make delivery of these a Completion deliverable.

### 1.16 Other disclosures (lease, Mossvale)
**Office lease (DD-007):** Notification obligation only; not described as requiring consent. Confirm the clause and give notice pre-Completion as a Seller covenant; low risk if accurately described.
**Mossvale (DD-009):** Restriction on assignment; share sale is not an assignment on the disclosed wording. Confirm there is no change-of-control provision elsewhere in the agreement; otherwise no action.

---

## 2. Summary of recommendations

**Threshold response**
1. Reject the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] categorisation and the statement that the limitation and disclosure packages are "agreed." All terms open; no authority has been given to accept any fallback.
2. Require a refreshed Disclosure Letter and updated source documents (the current letter is as at 22 September 2026).

**Non-negotiable / red-line points**
3. Express fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (1.5).
4. Separate Fundamental/Title warranty regime: 100% cap, six years minimum, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge/general disclosure (1.4).
5. Delete Clause 8.3 Buyer-knowledge exclusion in its entirety (1.7).
6. Delete general data-room and public-register disclosure; specific fair disclosure only (1.6).
7. Delete the "applies to all Claims" sweep and the "all Claims of any nature" extension; keep Title/Tax/IP/indemnity/payment/covenant regimes separate (1.3, 1.5, 1.14).

**Commercial counter-positions (hold at starting positions)**
8. General cap 25% / AUD 6,000,000 (1.1).
9. De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar recovery (1.2).
10. General claims period 24 months (1.3).
11. Tax and IP regimes marked OPEN with separate terms to be proposed (1.14).

**Conditions and completion mechanics**
12. Bluefen: CP requiring unconditional written consent plus evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, delivered before Completion; delete consent-on-delivery mechanic; strengthen endeavours obligation (1.8).
13. Riverlark: current payout letter, repayment from Completion funds via funds flow, executed security/PPSR releases and change-of-control waiver at Completion. Post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost sign-off (1.9).
14. DD-005 bonuses: AUD 420,000 plus quantified on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item, Debt/Transaction Expense deduction, or Seller indemnity (1.10).
15. Ironquay: Seller to procure payment of all SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment pre-Completion; broaden Clause 11.1 to cover failure of title to SOW3 materials; carve out of general regime; independently verify the open balance (1.11).
16. Title: Completion deliverables to include ASIC extract, PPSR searches, authorising resolutions, share certificates and no-encumbrance confirmation (1.15).

**Process / diligence points**
17. DD-006: log preservation, completed investigation, privacy advice on notification, written updates and close-out report pre-Completion; specific indemnity held open pending facts; do not accept the "not material" characterisation, and do not assert a breach either (1.12).
18. Sandbar: request agreements and renewal/termination details before classifying; no automatic Debt treatment or price deduction (1.13).
19. Lease / Mossvale: confirm clause wording; lease notice as Seller pre-Completion covenant (1.16).

**Authority reminder**
20. The two points where the Seller's numbers coincide with our fallbacks (20% cap; 18 months) remain unauthorised concessions. Any decision to move to them – ideally in exchange for the red-line points above – requires Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft.

I can turn this into a mark-up of the SPA clauses or a reply letter to Seller's counsel on request.
